archetypes.name: import-graph
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds a new cross-module import (pr_body -> tracking_issue) and makes a specific claim about the absence of a circular import; verifying this claim against actual file content is the highest-confidence guard against a silent import cycle introduced by the change.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect `python/tracking_issue.py`'s actual import block and compare it against the plan's claim that it imports only `config`, `gh`, `redact`, `errors`, `proc` — not `pr_body`. Trace each of those modules' own imports one level deep to confirm no transitive cycle exists. Check whether any future-work comment or open plan in the `python/` tree indicates `tracking_issue` will gain a `pr_body` dependency, which would invalidate the plan's no-cycle guarantee. Flag any discrepancy between the plan's stated import set and the file content. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: dead-surface
archetypes.rationale: The plan deletes PrBodyParts based on a claim of zero current and planned uses; an archetype that independently verifies this grep claim across the full python/ tree, docs, and bash scripts catches any reference the plan author missed.
archetypes.prompt_body: Search `python/pr_body.py`, `python/test_pr_body.py`, `python/test_tracking_issue.py`, and the broader `python/` directory for any import, instantiation, or attribute access of `PrBodyParts`. Also check `scripts/` and `docs/` for any bash or documentation reference to the dataclass by name. Verify the plan's assertion that `PrBodyParts` is never instantiated and referenced by no other open issue or committed plan. If any reference exists that contradicts the plan's claim, flag it as a gap between plan intent and repo evidence. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: layout-delta
archetypes.rationale: The plan silently shifts the PR-body blank-line layout (two blank lines before Closes #N to one) and claims no existing test pins the old format; an independent check of the test files and bash-side body assertions prevents a silent behavioral change from going undetected.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `python/test_pr_body.py` and `python/test_tracking_issue.py` and check whether any existing assertion pins the exact blank-line count before `Closes #N` in a composed PR body. Verify the plan's claim that no existing test pins the old two-blank-line layout against the actual test file content. Additionally, inspect `scripts/ship-pr.sh` around the Closes-line composition site to confirm the bash-side separator uses one blank line, validating the plan's claim that the new Python layout matches bash better. Flag any contradiction between the plan's layout-change claim and what the files actually assert or the bash side actually does. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
